It contains the decisions we made and should give that chat enough context to continue the schematic correctly.Plain textUPDATE TO MY ALTOIDS-TIN HANDHELD PCB DESIGN

I am building a FINAL custom PCB for a true standard-size Altoids-tin Binding of Isaac streaming handheld. This is not a prototype. IMPORTANT DESIGN CHANGE:
Instead of making a carrier PCB that mounts an RP2040-Zero module and MAX98357A breakout module, I want to integrate the BARE RP2040 and BARE MAX98357A directly onto my custom PCB. The PCB manufacturer can assemble the small SMD components like the RP2040, flash, MAX98357A, resistors, capacitors, regulator, etc. I do not plan on hand-soldering the RP2040 QFN.

==================================================
WHAT SHOULD BE DIRECTLY ON THE CUSTOM PCB
==================================================

1. BARE RP2040 CONTROLLER CIRCUIT

The RP2040 will be USB HID gamepad for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. Include the complete RP2040 support circuit based on the official Raspberry Pi RP2040 reference design:

- RP2040 IC
- External QSPI flash, around 2 MB is plenty
- 12 MHz crystal and required capacitors
- Required RP2040 decoupling capacitors
- Required power filtering
- Proper RP2040 1.1V core supply circuitry according to reference design
- 3.3V supply/regulation as needed
- USB D+ / D- circuitry
- Appropriate USB series resistors / protection according to reference design
- RUN/reset access
- BOOTSEL functionality
- SWD programming/debug pads:
 - SWDIO
 - SWCLK
 - GND
 - 3V3
- Useful test pads

The RP2040 firmware will make the PCB appear to the Pi as a standard USB game controller. Do NOT use a separate RP2040-Zero module anymore.

==================================================
2. Do NOT rely on cutting power to shut down normally because I want to avoid microSD corruption. Do NOT use a separate MAX98357A breakout board anymore. Display selected:

2.8-inch ILI9341 SPI TFT
320 × 240
Non-touch
SPI interface

The display will probably mount in the Altoids lid. Likely signals include:

- SPI SCK
- SPI MOSI
- CS
- DC
- RESET
- Backlight
- Power
- GND

MISO only needs to be included if required by the actual module/configuration. Do NOT attempt to recreate the Raspberry Pi circuitry on my PCB. Do NOT automatically design around a bulky:
Micro-USB OTG adapter -> USB-A cable -> USB-C cable. Instead, provide a compact PCB connector/pads for a very short USB connection between the custom PCB and Pi Zero 2 W. USB signals required:

- VBUS if needed
- D+
- D-
- GND

The Pi must operate as USB host and the RP2040 as USB device. Do not assume any particular Pi test pads or direct solder points until their exact function/pinout has been verified. POWER DISTRIBUTION ON THE CUSTOM PCB
==================================================

The custom PCB should distribute power but should NOT contain the actual high-current LiPo charger/5V boost converter for this first version. The external/proven power module will provide ~:

5V regulated
~2A continuous target
~10W
from a single-cell LiPo

That 5V enters the custom PCB. Selected battery:

EEMB LP103454
3.7V nominal
2000mAh
~ 34.5 × 56 × 10.3 mm
single-cell LiPo
protected/PCM version

The battery connects to the external charge/boost module. The PCB may include a JST-PH 2.0 interface only if it makes the physical design cleaner. Verify battery connector polarity before finalizing any JST footprint because LiPo JST polarity is not universally standardized.

==================================================
10. Do NOT integrate the high-current switching charger/boost circuit directly into the motherboard yet. Requirements for the module:

- 1S / 3.7V LiPo
- USB-C charging
- regulated 5V output
- about 2A continuous / ~10W
- preferably simultaneous charge/discharge
- preferably proper load sharing / power-path behavior
- overcharge protection
- over-discharge protection
- over-current protection
- short-circuit protection
- compact, ideally <= ~30 × 25 mm
- optional external enable/button is useful

Current candidate is a Cermant-style 1S USB-C charge/boost module claiming:
5V–5.15V / 2A output
2.4A charging
~92.5% efficiency
simultaneous charging/discharging

The exact module is NOT finalized yet, so the PCB mounting/interface should preferably not depend on a weird proprietary footprint unless we lock the module down first.

==================================================
11. Therefore:

- no exposed PCB pads/traces should be allowed to touch the tin
- PCB will eventually sit in a thin 3D-printed insulating tray or on insulating standoffs
- account for screw/standoff/mounting locations
- keep components away from the rounded internal corners
- minimize component height
- avoid unnecessary pin headers
- direct soldering or low-profile connectors are preferred
- modules/components should generally be mounted flat
- keep tall components away from the Pi/heatsink/battery overlap areas

Approximate starting board size:
88 × 52 mm

Do not finalize the board outline until actual internal tin measurements/component placement are available.

==================================================
17. COMPONENTS THAT SHOULD NO LONGER BE SEPARATE MODULES
==================================================

DO NOT buy/use:

- RP2040-Zero breakout board
- MAX98357A breakout board
- separate button perfboard
- large internal Dupont wiring harnesses

These functions are now being integrated directly onto the PCB.

==================================================
18. COMPONENTS THAT REMAIN SEPARATE
==================================================

Still separate:

- Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
- 2.8" ILI9341 SPI display
- EEMB LP103454 2000mAh LiPo
- 5V/2A charge/boost module
- 20mm 8-ohm speaker
- microSD card
- Pi heatsink
- 3D-printed controls/internal mounting pieces
- Altoids tin

==================================================
19. Do NOT optimize cost by taking unnecessary risks with LiPo charging or high-current switching power circuitry. For the first integrated motherboard, the RP2040 and audio circuit should be integrated, but the high-current LiPo charge/boost converter should remain a proven external module. When continuing the KiCad schematic, start with the RP2040 core/reference circuit, power, QSPI flash, crystal, SWD/BOOT/RUN, and USB interface. After that add Pi connections, display SPI, MAX98357A/I2S audio, shutdown circuitry, and finally external power/module connections.One particularly important update for that other chat is: don't design around the RP2040-Zero or MAX98357A breakout footprints anymore.
